newsitem.title: USA: USDA ups 96/97 world coffee crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: USDA ups 96/97 world coffee crop forecast.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday forecast 1996/97 world green coffee production at 100.9 million 60-kilogram bags, up 1.8 million from its estimate of 99.1 million in June.
The 1996/97 crop forecast would be up 12 percent from a revised estimate of 89.9 million bags harvested last season but shy of the record 103.7 million bags harvested in 1991/92, USDA said.
In its monthly World Agricultural Production report, the department revised down its 1996/97 Brazil coffee estimate to 27.0 million bags from 27.5 million bags forecast in June.
The department cut its forecast for Colombia's 1996/97 coffee output to 12.5 million bags from 13.0 million bags seen in June.
In the report, USDA upped its estimate for Indonesia's coffee crop to 7.5 million bags from 6.5 million bags and noted the current forecast was up 21 percent from last season's drought-reduced crop.
Mexico's output was pegged at 5.4 million bags, up from 4.7 million forecast in June. The forecast for Costa Rica's coffee crop was revised slightly to 2.5 million bags from 2.55 million.
USDA increased its estimate for Guatemala's output to 3.93 million bags from 3.5 million bags forecast in June.
The department also raised its estimate for Vietnam's 1996/97 coffee crop to 4.3 million bags from 3.5 million bags seen previously.
